(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice B M Shyam Prasad)
The appellants are the parents of the deceased, Mr. Sanath Rao, who has died in a road accident on 27.06.2018 when he was on his motorcycle.
The accident involves a lorry bearing No.KA-05-AC-6218.

The appellants have filed their claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.1 Crore in M.V.C. No.3657/2019 on the file of the III Additional Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru [for short, 'the Tribunal'].
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.17,50,200/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum apportioning this between the appellants NC: 2025:KHC:39641-DB HC-KAR in the ratio of 40:60.

The Tribunal has awarded the aforesaid amount under the following heads:
 Compensation Compensation  Heads Amount  Towards loss of dependency Rs.16,63,200-00  Towards loss of consortium Rs.44,000-00  Towards loss of estate Rs.16,500-00  Towards funeral & Rs.16,500-00  obsequies ceremony  expenses  Towards transportation of Rs.10,000-00  dead body  Total Rs.17,50,200-00 3.

Mr. K. Shantharaj, the learned counsel for the appellants, and Mr. Ashok N. Patil, the learned counsel who is on record for the first respondent [the Insurer of the lorry in question], are categorical that there is no dispute [a] that the lorry driver was negligent and responsible for the accident, [b] that the first respondent is liable to pay just and reasonable compensation to the appellants, and [c] that the deceased, who was aged 21 years as of the date of the accident, was studying for Engineering Graduation in NC: 2025:KHC:39641-DB HC-KAR Electronics and Communication with M/s. National Institute of Engineering, Mysuru.

4. Mr. K. Shantharaj submits that this Court must enhance compensation towards loss of dependency and towards loss of consortium, and in this regard, the learned counsel submits that the Tribunal has computed the loss of dependency taking the deceased's income at Rs.11,000/- per month with addition of 40% towards future prospects and deduction of 50% towards personal expenditure.
The learned counsel emphasises that the deceased had completed three semesters in distinction and was pursuing the fourth semester and that he had a bright future.

3 compensation towards loss of consortium, the Tribunal has only awarded a sum of Rs.44,000/-
when it is undisputed that each of the appellants would be entitled for such amount with an addition of 10% for every three years.

sentences.text: NC: 2025:KHC:39641-DB HC-KAR 5.

Mr. Ashok N. Patil submits that he will not contest that both the appellants are entitled for the loss of consortium in a sum of Rs.40,000/- and that there must be an enhancement in the loss of dependency taking a higher notional income of the deceased.

However, the learned counsel submits that the notional income cannot be taken at more than Rs.20,000/- per month; and in this regard,
the learned counsel relies upon a recent decision of the Apex Court in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No(s).28062-63/2023 underscoring that the Apex Court has taken the income of a deceased Engineering student at Rs.20,000/- per month.

6. In the light of the rival submissions, the only question for consideration is:
Should the Tribunal's judgment and award be modified granting higher compensation to the appellants towards loss of dependency and the loss of consortium?
NC: 2025:KHC:39641-DB HC-KAR 7.

The crucial evidence that remains undisputed is that the deceased, Mr. Sanath Rao, was pursuing Engineering with M/s. National Institute of Engineering, Mysuru [a prestigious Engineering Institution in the State of Karnataka], which lends for a just inference on the deceased being a meritorious student.
This gains further significance in the light of the undisputed fact that the deceased had passed the first three semesters in distinction.
Definitely, the Tribunal could not have taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month.

In the case of unskilled labour,
for computation of loss of dependency when the claim petitions arise out of the accidents in the year 2018, income is taken at Rs.12,500/- per month.

8. If the decision of the Apex Court is applied, the income of the deceased, Mr. Sanath Rao, NC:
2025:KHC:39641-DB HC-KAR must be taken at Rs.20,000/- with a just escalation of 10% because the accident in the present case is in the year 2018.
However, the distinguishing features are that the deceased was pursuing Engineering in Electronics and Communication as a meritorious student in a prestigious Institution in the State.
In the case on hand with the Apex Court, the deceased was pursuing a degree in Food Technology, and there is no reference to circumstances that would bear resemblance to the afore.

If the notional income of the deceased is taken at Rs.25,000/- per month,
there would be just compensation, and this will not cause any bonanza, which is frowned upon by the Courts.
9. As such, the loss of dependency is computed taking the notional income of the deceased, Sri Sanath Rao at Rs.25,000/- retaining all other parameters.
The loss of dependency will be in a sum NC: 2025:KHC:39641-DB HC-KAR of Rs.37,80,000/- determined in the following manner.
